title: Design Singly Linked List
description:
Design and implement your own linked list class `MyLinkedList` (using singly or doubly linked nodes) that supports 0-indexed operations:
- `MyLinkedList()` initializes an empty linked list.
- `int get(int index)` returns the value of the `index`-th node, or `-1` if `index` is out of bounds.
- `void addAtHead(int val)` inserts a node with value `val` before the first element.
- `void addAtTail(int val)` appends a node with value `val` as the last element.
- `void addAtIndex(int index, int val)` inserts a node with value `val` before the `index`-th node. If `index == length`, appends at the tail. If `index < 0` or `index > length`, does nothing.
- `void deleteAtIndex(int index)` deletes the `index`-th node if `0 <= index < length`; otherwise does nothing.
constraints: At most 2000 calls will be made to get, addAtHead, addAtTail, addAtIndex, and deleteAtIndex.
hints: Using a doubly linked list with sentinel `head` and `tail` dummy nodes plus a `size` counter eliminates edge cases at both ends.
To reach any valid `index` in O(min(index, size - index)), walk forward from `head` if `index < size / 2` and backward from `tail` otherwise.

examples.explanation: After addAtHead(1), addAtTail(3), addAtIndex(1, 2) the list is [1, 2, 3]; get(1) is 2; deleteAtIndex(1) leaves [1, 3]; get(1) is 3.
Out-of-bounds get/delete calls safely return -1 or do nothing; valid inserts at head/tail work as expected.
Deleting the sole element empties the list so subsequent get(0) returns -1.
